title: Other rivers' July flow gave no clear late-season low-flow prediction gain at three Arctic gauges in 1980-2011
abstract: We tested whether July flow in two other rivers improves a local August-October low-flow estimate after local July flow and a time trend are known. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 at Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. Fits used earlier common certified years from 1936. In 31 test years in 1980-2011, added cross-river flow reduced pooled squared log error by 2.25%. Conditional 95% three-year block limits were -14.49% to +13.94%. All planned checks had limits that included zero. Thus these models gave no clear added gain. Separate gauge point gains differed. This does not show independent rivers or no shared weather effect. Short records, common-year selection, revised data, regulation and conditional uncertainty limit the result. The package gives code, exact source hashes, aggregate scores, bootstrap draws, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit. External raw and record-level data remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Added cross-river July flow: error reduction and conditional 95% paired-year block limits. Positive values mean lower error.

citations.reason: Extends the local seasonal prediction question to information from other rivers. Same source and test years; new code and common training-year rule.
Shared spring timing context; not independent data.
